name: Fighter Valiant Commander
body:
Leaders come in many forms, some lead from the back where they can see the battlefield and plan, the valiant commander leads from the front, rallying the troops.

Mettle (Ex)

At 1st level, a valiant commander gains a Mettle pool that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to their Charisma modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day. But the valiant commander may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum.

The valiant commander may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits.

As an immediate action they may gain a bonus equal to their Constitution modifier on the next non-Fortitude saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn.
As part of making a Strength or Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Constitution bonus on that check. The valiant commander may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways.
If they use the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without their action
If the valiant commander uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the their action

If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.

Test of Valor (Ex)

At 1st level, the valiant commander expends a point of Mettle to issue a challenge as a free action to any creature that has an Intelligence score of 5 or greater. It must be intelligent enough to have a sense of pride, honor, and/or narcissism. It need not share a language with the valiant commander, as many creatures can understand a challenge and recognize a threat. This creature must be of a CR no less than the valiant commander’s character level – 2.

While this challenge lasts, the valiant commander gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls, and damage rolls. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter these bonuses each increase by an additional +1.

The test of valor lasts until the valiant commander or the target falls to 0 or fewer hit points or combat ends because either them or the target have surrendered honestly.

If a cowardly knave surrenders as a trick, the valiant commander does not need to spend another point of Mettle to regain the bonuses of the effect. The challenge resumes with renewed fervor because the target has attempted to take advantage of your honor or reputation. When this happens the bonuses from the original challenge are doubled. This automatic regaining of your test of valor bonuses can only occur within the first hour after combat ends.

This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.

Trial by Combat (Ex)

At 54th level, the valiant commander can shout a challenge to all enemies within 100 feet that can both see and hear them as a standard action. This appeals to the enemy’s pride, narcissism, fear, anger or other emotions and paints the valiant commander as a threat to be vanquished. This only affects enemies who would be subject to the valiant commander’s test of valor ability and expends a point of Mettle to activate. Each enemy to be affected must make a Will save equal to 10 + 1/2 the valiant commander’s class level + their Charisma modifier.

Each enemy that fails must attack the valiant commander or include them in the area of effect of a spell or special ability that doesn’t target creatures.

An enemy under the effects of trial by combat can choose not to attack valiant commander and instead spend a standard action calming their emotions and rolling a new save. Otherwise, trial by combat lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the valiant commander’s class levels + their Charisma modifier.

If the valiant commander is rendered unconscious by damage taken from targets under the effect of trial by combat, they restore two points of Mettle.

This ability replaces the weapon training gained at 5th level.

Always Ready (Ex)

At 7th level, whenever the valiant commander rolls for initiative they gain 2 bonus points of Mettle that exceeds their normal maximum. This Mettle is spent first if the valiant commander uses any abilities which require Mettle. If they spend no Mettle before the end of combat these bonus points disappear when combat ends. The bonus points of Mettle gained increases to 3 at 13th level and to 4 at 19th level. This ability does not stack with other instances of this ability, however, any class that provides this ability is added to the effective class level to determine the amount of bonus Mettle.

Call to Action (Ex)

At 8th level, the valiant commander gains the ability to rouse the minds and bodies of their allies. By spending a point of Mettle as a move action they can shout a word of encouragement and inspiration to their allies. All allies within 100 feet that can see and hear the valiant commander may immediately make a new saving throw against any mind-affecting ability, ability that impedes their movement, or ability that limits the kinds of actions they can take on their turn (this also grants a new check to escape a grapple, though this isn’t a saving throw).

The ally gains a bonus on this new roll equal to the valiant commander’s Charisma bonus. If this new roll is successful the effect is treated as though the ally had succeeded on their original save. The valiant commander regains an amount of Mettle equal to the number of allies who succeeded their check or save, up to their Charisma modifier.

This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 8th level.

Death Before Dishonor (Ex)

At 11th level, the valiant commander gains Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. At any time while the Diehard feat is active, the valiant commander may expend a point of Mettle to suppress the staggered condition for the round. Any strenuous action still causes damage as normal.

Additionally, if the valiant commander’s hit points are below their Constitution score, they may expend a point of Mettle each round to continue to act under the Diehard feat until they reach a negative hp total equal to their valiant commander class levels plus their Constitution score. During this time, they may still expend additional Mettle to suppress the staggered condition.

If the valiant commander does not expend Mettle while still within this threshold, they are considered dying and stable for one round. If they do not receive healing within the round to bring their hit points back above their Constitution score, they die.

This replaces the armor training gained at 11th level.

To Arms (Ex)

At 13th level, the valiant commander has learned to truly lead by example. As a full-round action that costs 2 points of Mettle, the valiant commander may make a single attack against an enemy.

If it hits, this attack is treated as the feat Vital Strike, and each ally within 60 feet who can see and hear you is granted an attack of opportunity on a target they threaten or a target within the first range increment of a ranged or thrown weapon they are currently wielding.

This ability allows allies with ranged weapons to make an attack of opportunity when they normally could not. This ability benefits from the Improved Vital Strike and better feats.

This ability replaces the weapon training at 13th level.

Overwhelming Presence (Ex)

At 16th level, as a swift action the valiant commander may spend 2 points of Mettle to project their superior skill and strength of arms to all enemies, weeding out the weak and allowing only the strong to face them. All enemies within 60 feet of the valiant commander must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 their class levels + their Charisma modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat.

Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more or has fewer HD than the valiant commander’s character level minus 4 is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken as long as they can see and hear the valiant commander. Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken.

This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 16th level.
